document.title: What changed: compare a refreshed review with the previous one
document.summary: `refresh` keeps the old review beside the new one, and `serve` and `export` send a `changes` payload that the new What changed page shows. Separately, the hosted `api/review.json` now holds the document in its on-disk form, so the skill's hosted Refresh path can save it back.
document.why: When a review is rewritten for the same change, the human may want to see how grouping and claims shifted ([#72](source:s1)).

sources.title: Compare review regenerations (wired previous→current, not bare two-file CLI)
sources.gist: Show how groups, lookFor, sources, and summaries changed between two review documents for the same change, without a second code diff.

sources.label: Claude Code session · Oct 22
sources.gist: The user picked a quiet What changed page out of several UX options, then asked to fix the hosted Refresh bug and to add tests that stop this kind of bug.

lookFor: Done differently: [#72](source:s1) asks to show regrouping as hunk membership shifts. The page lists files that moved in or out of a group and counts new, changed, and reformatted hunks per group; it does not list which hunk moved between two groups inside one file.

The page is reachable only from a link at the end of the Overview kicker, the `h` key, and the `#changes` hash, as asked in the [session](source:s2). A review that was never refreshed shows none of them.

parts.name: What changed
parts.summary: Keep the previous review, compare it with the current one, and show the result on its own page.

parts.name: Hosted document
parts.summary: Make the hosted `api/review.json` document a valid `review.json` again.

groups.title: refresh keeps the previous review
groups.why: The comparison needs the old document after `refresh` overwrites `review.json` ([#72](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `cmdRefresh` copies the old file to `review.<short head sha>.json` beside it and names that file in the new optional `previous` field; the CLI prints where it went.
lookFor: Each `refresh` that changes the review leaves one more `review.<sha>.json` in the same directory. Nothing deletes the older ones.

groups.title: The changes payload
groups.why: The UI is fixed and only data changes, so the comparison is computed on the server side and sent with the review ([#72](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `openReview` loads the `previous` file next to the review path, and `changesPayload` compares prose, lookFor, sources, and group files by group id, with hunk counts from `matchHunks` over the old range.
lookFor: Groups match by `id`. A group whose id changed shows as one removed and one new group, even when its hunks are the same.
A missing previous file gives no `changes` at all. A previous file that exists but does not parse makes `openReview` throw, so `serve` and `export` stop.
When git no longer has the old commits, `codeChanges` returns nothing and the page shows the text changes without hunk counts.

groups.title: export opens the review from its path
groups.why: `export` loaded the document itself and passed it in, so `openReview` could not find the `previous` file and the exported site had no `changes`.
groups.summary: `exportStaticSite` drops its `ctx` option, always opens the review from `dataPath`, and returns the context it used; the CLI, the eval runner, and the tests take it from the result, and a refresh test runs export and the `jq .document` round trip end to end.
lookFor: `export` now prints the drift and coverage warnings after it writes the site, with the note `exported anyway`.
The two edits in `image.test.ts` and `lockfile.test.ts` are identical.

groups.title: The What changed page
groups.why: The user asked for a comparison that stays out of the way and opens only when intended ([session](source:s2)).
groups.summary: A new `changes` selection renders `Changes.tsx`, reached from a link in the Overview kicker, the `h` key in `App.tsx`, and the `#changes` hash, which falls back to the Overview when the review has no `changes`.

groups.title: The skill gives the #changes URL
groups.why: After a refresh the user should land on the comparison, not search for it.
groups.summary: Refresh step 5 tells the agent to end the URL with `#changes`. `.agents/skills/comprehende/SKILL.md` is a synced copy of the `skills-next` file; read one.

groups.title: Generated schema JSON
groups.why: The JSON schema is generated from `src/schema/review.ts` and copied into the skill.
groups.summary: The three files are identical and add the `previous` property. Skip them; `keep-previous` holds the source.

groups.title: Hosted api/review.json holds the on-disk document
groups.why: The hosted Refresh path saves `api/review.json` `.document` as `review.json`, but its hunk refs were parsed objects, so the schema rejected it ([session](source:s2)).
groups.summary: `reviewPayload` sends `storedDocument(document)` typed as `StoredReviewDocument`, the UI parses the ref strings back in `fetchReview` with `parseStoredHunkRef` (moved from the schema to `identity.ts`), and `agent-md` lists the strings as they are.
lookFor: Breaking: sites exported before this change still hold object hunk refs. `jq .document` from them still fails `validate` until the site is exported again.

commits.subject: Add a What changed page that compares a refreshed review with the previous one
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
refresh keeps the old review.json beside the new one under its head SHA and
names it in `previous`. serve and export load it and send `changes`: prose,
lookFor, sources, and per-group hunk counts from matchHunks. The UI shows them
on #changes, linked from the Overview kicker and the `h` key. Nothing shows
for a review that was never refreshed.

Fix the hosted Refresh path: api/review.json held parsed hunk refs (objects),
so `jq .document > review.json` failed the schema. The payload now holds the
on-disk form and the UI parses refs when it loads. exportStaticSite always
opens the review from its path, so it cannot be handed a context without
`previous`. A test runs refresh, export, and the jq round trip end to end.

Closes #72

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
